input: Find founder- or family-owned US veterinary clinic groups with 5-30 locations

companies.hq: Watertown, MA, US (380 Pleasant St, Watertown, MA 02472; five hospitals across greater Boston, MA and Warwick, RI)
companies.name: Callanan Veterinary Group
companies.traction: 2026 marks the group's 100-year centennial; AVMA employer profile states 'We are the oldest privately owned veterinary group in the country'; testimonials cite clients of 40+ years; internship program with University of Pennsylvania
companies.employees: ~150 employees (AVMA employer profile, as_of 2026); LinkedIn company size 51-200 employees
companies.ownership: Family-owned - 'family-owned and operated since 1926'; 'the oldest family-owned private veterinary hospital group in America'; four generations of Callanans; today run by Dr. Jon Callanan (Chief Medical Officer) and family members Neil, Charles and Joseph
companies.rank_reason: Purest thesis fit: fourth-generation family ownership since 1926, explicitly family-owned (not a consolidator), 5 locations squarely in the 5-30 band, 100-year operating history and ~150 employees - a rare centennial independent that has never sold.
companies.headcount_growth: Four hospitals by 2006 (Brighton 1976, Neponset 1991, Union Square 1994, RI Animal Medical Center 2003, Massachusetts Animal Medical Center 2006) grew to five hospitals with the 2022 opening of Wellington Circle Veterinary Center, Medford; ~150 employees as of 2026 (AVMA profile)

criteria_evidence.evidence: 'Founded in 1926, Callanan Veterinary Group is the oldest family-owned private veterinary hospital group in America'; four generations of one family, currently led by Dr. Jon Callanan

Five full-service hospitals: Wellington Circle Veterinary Center (Medford, MA), Massachusetts Animal Medical Center (Watertown, MA), Neponset Animal Hospital (Dorchester/Boston, MA), Somerville Veterinary Center (Somerville, MA), Rhode Island Animal Medical Center (Warwick, RI)
Privately held US veterinary hospital group headquartered in Watertown, MA with locations in Massachusetts and Rhode Island; ~150 employees per AVMA employer profile

companies.hq: Clinton Township, MI, US (42822 Garfield Road, Clinton Township, MI 48038)
companies.name: Veterinary United
companies.traction: Acquired Waverly Animal Hospital of Lansing, MI (Calder Capital-advised transaction); consolidated 8 PIMS systems into one Digitail cloud platform across the network; 2026 class of Purina Nutrition Ambassadors
companies.employees: Over 400 employees (company bio page, as_of 2026); LinkedIn range 201-500 employees
companies.ownership: Family-owned - began as a family business by Dr. Thomas Bankstahl and his wife Julie; Dr. Bankstahl is listed as 'Visionary, Owner, Team Leader, CEO'; private-equity tracking list Private Equity Vet records the owner as 'Thomas Bankstahl and family'; describes itself as 'more than a group of practices - we're a family'
companies.rank_reason: Largest qualifying family-owned group: 22+ practices plus boarding/grooming centers run by the founding Bankstahl family since 1999, 400+ employees, still acquiring (Waverly, 2025) - family-owned scale with real M&A traction.
companies.headcount_growth: 22 practices + 4 boarding/daycare/grooming centers as of Dec 2023 (Digitail customer story) grew to 26 mapped US listings including newly acquired Waverly Animal Hospital as of Oct 24, 2026 (Private Equity Vet); site locations page lists ~30 hospitals/resorts incl. two Florida practices; 400+ employees

criteria_evidence.evidence: Founded 27 years ago as a family business by Dr. Thomas Bankstahl and his wife Julie; 'Our family of hospitals all support each other'; PEVet ownership column: 'Thomas Bankstahl and family'
'A practice group of 22 practices' plus 4 boarding/daycamp/grooming centers in southeastern Michigan (26 mapped listings incl. Waverly per Private Equity Vet, Oct 24 2026)
Southeastern Michigan veterinary hospital group, HQ Clinton Township, MI; 'vet-owned and vet-centric company'; 400+ employees

companies.hq: Hunterdon County / Chatham area, New Jersey, US (hospitals in Flemington, Whitehouse Station, Lebanon, Bedminster and Chatham, NJ)
companies.name: Symbios Animal Health
companies.traction: Grew from 3 practices to a family of 6 NJ animal hospitals; opened a first-of-its-kind concierge veterinary practice on Main Street in Chatham (TAPinto coverage); high client review volumes (e.g., Hunterdon Hills ~309 Google reviews, South Branch ~250)
companies.ownership: Family-owned by working veterinarians - '100% independently and family owned' with 'no corporate parent and no outside investors'; owners are Dr. Nick Pope and Dr. Elizabeth Pope (husband and wife, OSU veterinary graduates) and Dr. Jan Cailles
companies.rank_reason: Textbook founder/family thesis fit - two veterinarian spouses and a partner own all six hospitals outright with explicitly 'no outside investors'; growth financed through bank debt (Firstrust), not equity; only gap is undisclosed headcount and no stated founding year for the group.
companies.headcount_growth: 3 New Jersey practices (South Branch, Clover Hill, Symbios) when profiled by Firstrust Bank grew to 6 animal hospitals incl. the new Chatham concierge practice as of 2026

criteria_evidence.evidence: Drs. Nick and Elizabeth Pope (married veterinarians) and Dr. Jan Cailles own the group; site states '100% independently and family owned... no corporate parent and no outside investors'

A family of six New Jersey animal hospitals: Clover Hill (Flemington), Hunterdon Hills (Whitehouse Station), Oldwick (Whitehouse Station), South Branch (Lebanon), Bedminster Veterinary Healthcare (Bedminster), Symbios Chatham

companies.headcount_growth: 8 clinics when James Rericha was interviewed on The Vet'd podcast grew to 10 clinics across Missouri on the current r.vet site (as_of 2026)

10 clinics across Missouri: Lake of the Ozarks, Laurie, Cross Creek (Waynesville), Columbia, All Creatures-Bolivar, Ashland, Westside (Jefferson City), Romaine Creek (Fenton), Kirbyville, Lebanon

output.search_notes: Method: the Private Equity Vet corporate-ownership list (15,164 practices; database updated Oct 24, 2026) was used as the ownership-exclusion and candidate roster, cross-checked against companies' own sites, AVMA/BBB registries, local press and LinkedIn. Nine founder- or family-owned US veterinary clinic groups with 5-30 locations were verified: Callanan Veterinary Group, Veterinary United, Symbios Animal Health, R Veterinary, Cara Veterinary, Emergency Veterinary Care Centers, PetWellClinic, Pet Cure Inc. and BoosterPet. Excluded after verification: (1) PE- or corporate-backed groups of similar size per the same list - Sploot (L Catterton, 20), Doppler Veterinary Network (Lindsay Goldberg, 29), Lovet (The Aspen Group, 28), Modern Animal/Chewy Vet Care (Chewy, 30/25), Lakefield (Desmarais/Peloton, 84), Small Door (Valspring, 13), VetnCare (Great Point, 15), Hometown (Briarcliff, 14), O'Brien Veterinary Group (The Cambria Group investment firm, 24), Associated Veterinary Partners (minority growth investment from Swift Anchor Holdings since 2022, vet co-ownership, 25 mapped hospitals); (2) NewDay Veterinary Care / Pet Paradise (25 vet listings) - majority-owned by Crane Group since June 2016, a Columbus OH family-owned holding company the Jacksonville press describes as an investment firm, whose company-wide footprint is 60+ resorts across 11 states with veterinary services at 20+ of them, so it fails both the 5-30 clinic-group framing and clean founder/family ownership; (3) The Vets Pets (36 locations) and Curo Pet Care (69) exceed the 30-location cap; CAPNA (~92% veterinarian-owned, 17 practices at 2010 founding) could not be verified as still independent at 5-30 scale today. Main gaps: Symbios group founding year and headcount, Pet Cure founder documentation and headcount growth, and exact employee totals for most smaller groups are not published; headcount growth is given as dated location counts where staff counts were unavailable.
